provenance: 사용자가 직접 그렸다고 제공한 스케치를 기준으로 생성. 첨부 원본은 변경하지 않고 사본을 보관.
direction: 긴 얼굴, 눌러쓴 모자와 오른쪽으로 긴 챙, 팬 볼, 좁은 눈, 넓은 어깨를 우선 반영. 거친 도트풍. 팔 자세는 양팔꿈치가 책상 위에 닿도록 후속 보정.

별의 디지털 위장무늬는 v3 디자인 요구 유지. 이번 이미지는 캐릭터만 검토.
사용자 피드백 전 게임 그래픽 적용 보류. 웹 빌드 별도 승인 대기.
prompt:
Use case: sketch-to-render, LOW-RES PIXEL ART, not realism.
Input image 1: the user's own original drawing. This drawing is the authoritative character design, silhouette, pose and facial proportions. Convert THIS DRAWING into a colored, coarse pixel-art military game opponent. Preserve its distinctive awkward shapes. Do not replace it with a conventional handsome soldier, a different caricature or a polished anime illustration.

Single character, front view, complete upper body behind a simple plain rectangular desk, framed like the drawing, on a clean white/off-white background. Keep the sketch's narrow long head, deep cap, very broad angular shoulders, thin neck, and inward-bending arms with elbows planted on the desk near the center. Follow the drawn arm angles and large triangular spaces inside the bent arms. Keep both elbows visibly supported on the table; simple small hands, no crossed arms, no hero pose. No second character, no phone screen, no game board, no labels or other decorative objects. Portrait or nearly square composition.

Important design fidelity:
- The cap has a tall rounded crown pulled LOW over the eyes and a long brim projecting conspicuously to the VIEWER'S RIGHT, exactly as in the sketch. Small plain rectangular cap patch. It is a soft military cap, not a helmet.
- The face is vertically LONG AND NARROW, with a slightly lopsided slab-like chin and angular hollow cheeks. Follow the sketch's head outline rather than creating a huge nose or round head. No bulging ears or glamorous hair.
- Tiny, narrow, jagged eyes mostly shaded by the cap brim. Heavy sharp eyebrows, glaring in an extremely bad mood. Put just one or two hot orange/yellow logical pixels in each eye to suggest smoldering competitiveness, not huge eyeballs or literal flames.
- Nose is long, thin and angular, nearly one crooked line, as drawn. Mouth is a tiny crooked downward grimace. Strong deep hollow-cheek planes and a few angular short dark strokes along BOTH lower cheeks, based on the sketch, to look gaunt and disgruntled, not wounded.
- This recruit is funny because of his strangely serious, sour expression and exaggerated mismatched proportions: very wide shoulders, narrow long neck and skinny long face. Original, comically unattractive, distinctive. No cheerful smile, no heroic beauty.
- Clothing is a simple short-sleeve digital-camouflage T-shirt and matching patrol cap. Invented camouflage built from a FEW LARGE olive/khaki square clusters. No real unit insignia, national flags or branded patterns.
- Desk is flat, plain olive-brown, following the sketch's broad rectangle. No woodgrain detail, books, mugs or equipment.

Pixel treatment must be markedly simpler than a detailed painted pixel illustration: construct the entire character on an approximately 128×144 logical-pixel grid, enlarged with crisp nearest-neighbor square edges. A face about 24–32 logical pixels wide. Around 12–16 flat colors, skin in only three tones, dark chunky stepped outlines, big flat graphic planes. No gradients, airbrush, anti-aliasing, smooth curves, noisy micro-camouflage, detailed musculature, glints or fine texture. Sparse carefully placed pixels and bold silhouettes. Draw a sprite, not an illustration with a pixel filter. The user's drawn distinctive shape and expression take priority over realism or prettification.
pose_edit_prompt:
Edit ONLY the arm pose and the top surface of the desk in this pixel-art character image. Keep the face, displeased expression, glowing narrow eyes, gaunt cheek lines, long thin nose, elongated head, low crooked cap, broad angular shoulders, camouflage, coarse pixel size, colors, background and framing unchanged. Do not beautify or redesign him.

The current hands press down on the desk and both elbows are above it. Correct this: BOTH ELBOWS themselves must rest visibly on the desk, with forearms bent about 90 degrees and lying across the tabletop, and both hands resting loosely near the middle. He leans forward into a tense board-game opponent pose. Place the left elbow toward the left side of the desk and the right elbow toward the right side, with forearms extending inward across its top toward the hands. Show upper arms connecting shoulders to the elbows, clear bends, no crossed arms. The two elbow contact points must be visible. Add only enough plain tabletop depth to support both forearms. No extra furniture or props. Maintain the sketch-inspired wide shoulders and narrow gaunt face. Entire upper body and both arms visible. Keep the same deliberately simple blocky low-resolution sprite treatment.
